The Best Naked Bike Riding Gear UK Riders Need

The best naked bike riding gear in the UK is built around one central truth: with no fairing to hide behind, the wind is your constant companion. A roadster or streetfighter is a joy in town and on a twisty B-road, but push past 60mph and the windblast tugs at your shoulders, worms into any gap in your kit and slowly wears you out. The right gear turns that exposure from a liability into part of the fun, giving you versatile, breathable protection you can adjust as the day and the weather change.

Naked bikes are the natural all-rounders, equally at home commuting through the week and blasting the Cat and Fiddle or the A5 through Snowdonia at the weekend. Your gear should be just as versatile. If you want to stretch a roadster into longer trips, our guide on how to tour on a naked bike pairs neatly with the kit advice here.

Understanding Windblast and How Gear Fights It

On a naked bike the wind hits your chest and shoulders directly, and at speed it pulls at loose fabric until you are tensing your core just to hold position. Two things fight this: a close, athletic cut that does not flap, and a layering system that lets you seal up when it is cold and open up when the blast is welcome cooling on a hot day. Baggy adventure jackets are the wrong shape here. You want kit that hugs the body and cuts a clean line into the air.

The Armoured Shirt: A Naked Bike Favourite

My single favourite piece of naked bike kit is the armoured riding shirt. It looks like a casual overshirt but carries CE armour at the shoulders, elbows and back, and it is close-fitting enough to shrug off windblast far better than a loose jacket. On warm days you can wear it alone, and when it turns cold you layer a shell over the top.

The Knox Venture Shirt is the piece that converts people. It is comfortable enough to forget you are wearing it, protective where it counts, and its slim cut means the wind has nothing to grab. For town riding and short summer blasts it is very hard to beat.

Summer Jackets: Airflow Without Sacrificing Safety

When the mercury climbs, a mesh or heavily vented summer jacket keeps you cool without leaving you unprotected. The trick is finding one with enough real airflow to work in a British heatwave yet enough armour and abrasion resistance to matter in a fall. The Rev'It Eclipse 2 Summer Jacket flows genuine air across the chest and back, which is exactly what you want when you are stuck in warm town traffic on a naked bike with no fairing to duck behind. Our guide to summer motorcycle jackets lines up the best of them.

A mesh jacket you actually wear on a hot day protects you far more than an armoured touring jacket left at home because it is too warm. The best gear is the gear you will keep on.

Riding Jeans: The Versatile Legwear Choice

Naked bikes suit a relaxed, do-anything wardrobe, and modern riding jeans fit that perfectly. Single-layer jeans woven with aramid or built from abrasion-resistant fibres like Cordura look like ordinary denim but offer real protection, and they take CE knee and hip armour. You can ride to the pub, walk in and look normal, which is the whole appeal of a roadster lifestyle.

I wear a pair of Furygan Jean 03 Riding Jeans for most of my naked bike riding, from commutes to weekend rideouts. For a proper comparison of single-layer versus lined jeans and how the ratings work, read our motorcycle riding jeans guide.

Gloves and Shoes for Everyday Versatility

The naked bike ethos is versatile kit you can live in, so I keep my glove and footwear choices practical.

  • Summer gloves. A vented leather glove such as the Held Air Stream Gloves keeps air moving over your hands without leaving them unprotected.
  • Riding shoes. Short protective trainers like the Alpinestars Faster-3 Shoes give ankle armour and a grippy sole while looking casual enough to wear off the bike.
  • Layer for weather. Keep a packable waterproof and a neck tube in the tail so a sudden shower does not end the ride.

Beating the Cold on an Exposed Bike

Without a fairing, cold weather bites harder on a naked bike, and your hands feel it first. A set of Oxford Heaterz Premium Heated Grips extends your riding season dramatically and lets you wear thinner, more tactile gloves on chilly mornings. Add a windproof base layer under your shirt and you can keep riding comfortably well into autumn on roads like Hartside on the A686 where the temperature drops fast with altitude.

Building a Kit for Your Naked Bike

The beauty of naked bike gear is that it flexes to how you ride. A commuter and weekend rider on a Kawasaki Z650 will love the armoured shirt and jeans combo for its everyday ease. If you lean towards sportier riding on something like a Kawasaki Ninja 650, you might want a closer-fitting jacket to cut through the wind. And a retro roadster rider on a Royal Enfield Interceptor 650 can happily embrace the relaxed, casual look while still wearing genuine protection underneath. Build around versatility, dress for the wind, and a naked bike will reward you as one of motorcycling's great all-rounders.

An armoured riding shirt is the naked bike favourite: casual looks with CE armour and a slim profile.
A well-vented mesh summer jacket you actually wear beats an armoured coat left at home.
Single-layer riding jeans give real protection and everyday off-bike practicality.
Heated grips and a windproof base layer extend the season on an exposed bike.
